questions.q: Which bones belong to the axial skeleton? (select all that apply)
questions.explain: The axial skeleton is the skull, vertebral column (including sacrum and coccyx), ribs and sternum; the girdles belong to the appendicular skeleton.

questions.q: Which carpals are in the DISTAL row? (select all that apply)
questions.explain: The distal row, lateral to medial, is trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate; scaphoid and lunate are in the proximal row.

questions.q: Which are classified as short bones? (select all that apply)
questions.explain: Short bones (carpals, tarsals) are about equal in all dimensions. The patella is sesamoid, vertebrae are irregular and metacarpals are long bones.

questions.q: Which are classified as flat bones? (select all that apply)
questions.explain: Flat bones are broad and thin with compact bone around cancellous bone, such as the scapula, sternum, ilium, ribs and skull bones.

questions.q: Which bony landmarks are projections where tendons and ligaments attach? (select all that apply)
questions.explain: Tuberosities, trochanters and crests are attachment sites. A fossa and foramen are depressions/openings; a facet is an articular surface.

questions.q: Which joints are biaxial? (select all that apply)
questions.explain: The wrist is ellipsoid and the thumb CMC is saddle, both biaxial. The elbow and atlantoaxial are uniaxial, the hip triaxial and intercarpals non-axial.

questions.q: Which structures are made of fibrocartilage? (select all that apply)
choices: Triangular fibrocartilage disc at the wrist
Articular surface of the femoral head
questions.explain: Fibrocartilage absorbs shock, deepens sockets and fills gaps. The ear is elastic cartilage and articular surfaces are hyaline.

questions.q: Which joints are pivot joints? (select all that apply)
questions.explain: Pivot joints are uniaxial and allow rotation, as at C1 on C2 and the radioulnar joints.

questions.q: Which statements about hyaline (articular) cartilage are true? (select all that apply)
choices: It repairs itself quickly after damage
It has no blood supply of its own
It covers bone ends in synovial joints
It gives the external ear its shape
It is nourished by synovial fluid
questions.explain: Hyaline cartilage is avascular and fed by synovial fluid, so it cannot repair itself; elastic cartilage shapes the ear.

questions.q: Which statements about ligaments are true? (select all that apply)
choices: They reinforce the outer fibrous layer of the joint capsule
An injury to a ligament is a strain
They are flexible but not elastic
An injury to a ligament is a sprain
questions.explain: Ligaments join bone to bone, bend but do not stretch, reinforce the capsule, and are sprained. Tendons join muscle to bone and are strained.

questions.q: Which statements about Osgood-Schlatter disease are correct? (select all that apply)
choices: It is a bacterial bone infection
It is related to the pull of the patellar tendon
It is avascular necrosis of the femoral head
It is an overuse condition of growing children and adolescents
It causes inflammation at the tibial tuberosity
questions.explain: Osgood-Schlatter is traction inflammation at the tibial tuberosity growth plate; avascular necrosis of the femoral head is Legg-Calve-Perthes.

questions.q: A client's goniometry results are listed below. Which values show a LIMITATION compared with normal ROM? (select all that apply)
questions.explain: Normals are shoulder abduction 0-180, knee flexion 0-135 and wrist extension 0-70; the other values match normal ranges.

questions.q: List the three structural types of joints. For each, give its functional name, how much motion and stability it allows, and one example.
questions.model: Fibrous (synarthrodial): no joint cavity, little or no motion and extreme stability, e.g., skull sutures. Cartilaginous (amphiarthrodial): bones joined by cartilage, slight motion and great stability, e.g., intervertebral joints or pubic symphysis. Synovial (diarthrodial): joint cavity enclosed in a capsule, the most motion and the least stability, e.g., shoulder, hip or knee.
points: Synovial = diarthrodial, most motion, least stability

questions.q: Compare osteoblasts and osteoclasts, and explain how an imbalance between them leads to osteoporosis.
questions.model: Bone is constantly remodeled (dynamic equilibrium). Osteoblasts build new bone and repair and remodel it; osteoclasts resorb, or break down, old bone. When osteoclast resorption outpaces osteoblast formation, bone mass and density are lost, bones become brittle and fracture easily, which is osteoporosis.
points: Osteoclast activity exceeding osteoblast activity = bone loss/osteoporosis

questions.q: Name and describe five parts of a long bone.
questions.model: Diaphysis: the tubular shaft. Epiphysis: each proximal and distal end. Metaphysis: the flared region between the shaft and the end. Epiphyseal (growth) plate: cartilage plate where a growing bone lengthens. Medullary cavity: central canal of the shaft holding marrow. Periosteum: outer covering rich in nerves and blood vessels.

questions.q: Classify each joint by synovial joint type and number of axes, and name one motion it allows: glenohumeral, humeroulnar (elbow), radiocarpal (wrist), thumb CMC.
questions.model: Glenohumeral: ball and socket, triaxial; flexion/extension, abduction/adduction and rotation. Humeroulnar: hinge, uniaxial; flexion and extension. Radiocarpal: ellipsoid (condyloid), biaxial; flexion/extension and radial/ulnar deviation. Thumb CMC: saddle, biaxial; flexion/extension and abduction/adduction, plus accessory rotation for opposition.

questions.q: Define goniometry. A client's elbow flexion measures 0-110 degrees. State the normal value and explain how this limitation could affect daily occupations.
questions.model: Goniometry is measurement of joint angles (ROM) with a goniometer, compared with normal ranges to find limitations. Normal elbow flexion is 0-150 degrees, so 0-110 is limited by about 40 degrees. The client may have trouble bringing the hand to the mouth or face for eating, drinking, brushing teeth, shaving or combing hair, and may compensate with neck flexion or adaptive equipment such as long-handled utensils.
